## AI news this week: August 3–8, 2026

The week’s main AI story was less about a blockbuster public model launch and more about **frontier labs positioning themselves for AI-assisted scientific research and possible self-improvement**.

### 1. Google DeepMind is emphasizing “post-chatbot” AI research

Demis Hassabis is reportedly moving away from day-to-day operational management to become Alphabet’s chief scientist and chair of Google DeepMind, with an emphasis on longer-term AGI research. The change comes as Hassabis and other leading AI executives increasingly describe the industry as approaching a threshold sometimes called the “singularity”—the point at which AI systems could materially accelerate their own development. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/newsletters/axios-am-e6e15a72-3b81-4056-9657-5c07f9825685?utm_source=openai))

**Why it matters:** This suggests that major labs are organizing around automated research, scientific discovery, and AGI strategy—not just consumer assistants and incremental model upgrades.

### 2. OpenAI briefed Washington officials on a more advanced system called “Astra”

OpenAI reportedly spent the previous week briefing U.S. officials on **Astra**, described as a more powerful system that has made substantial progress on longstanding problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science
